harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04). Installed aide/aide-common, verified the packaged Debian/Ubuntu AIDE config recursively applies full content checksums (SHA256/SHA512/RMD160/TIGER/HAVAL/GOST/CRC32 + metadata) to /etc via the "/ Full" catch-all rule (with narrow, pre-existing exceptions for known-volatile files like resolv.conf/adjtime), initialized the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db (70,149 entries), and proved detection works end-to-end by tampering with /etc/hosts, running aide --check, observing the exact checksum/size/mtime diff reported, then restoring /etc/hosts and re-baselining to a clean state. The distro's /etc/cron.daily/aide job (already enabled) will run these checks automatically going forward and report changes. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on node1: captured pre-restart boot_id and a clean /etc AIDE check, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (a1dc8e25... -> 2e616fe5...), and confirmed post-restart that the AIDE database file was intact (same md5) and a fresh aide --check showed zero differences under real /etc paths (all reported diffs were in /run, lxcfs cgroup pseudo-files from ephemeral SSH sessions, or postfix's chroot copies under /var/spool/postfix/etc, none in /etc itself).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/environment and confirmed AIDE package availability
Installed aide and aide-common via apt
Reviewed AIDE config (/etc/aide/aide.conf and aide.conf.d/*) to confirm /etc is covered by full content-checksum monitoring
Ran aideinit to build the initial AIDE database for /etc/ (and full filesystem) baseline
Verified the active database (/var/lib/aide/aide.db) matches the freshly generated one
Ran aide.wrapper --check to confirm a clean baseline with zero /etc differences
Tampered with /etc/hosts (appended a marker line) and re-ran aide.wrapper --check to prove detection of the change with full checksum diff output
Restored /etc/hosts to its original content and re-ran aideinit to re-baseline to the clean state
Confirmed /etc/cron.daily/aide (daily automated check+report) is present and cron.service is enabled/active
Captured pre-restart boot_id and a clean baseline check as restart evidence
Issued a backgrounded `sudo reboot` on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned after the restart
Verified boot_id changed post-restart, confirming a genuine reboot
Verified AIDE database file integrity (checksum) and cron service health post-restart
Ran a post-restart aide.wrapper --check and confirmed zero differences within real /etc paths

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and configured to monitor /etc with content-level integrity checks
evidence.summary: Confirmed Ubuntu 16.04 node1, installed aide/aide-common, and confirmed via aide.conf.d that /etc is monitored recursively with full checksums (SHA256/SHA512/etc.) via the top-level '/ Full' rule, with only known-volatile files (resolv.conf, adjtime, etc.) exempted.

evidence.requirement: Baseline database initialized and in place at the configured active path
evidence.summary: Ran aideinit; produced /var/lib/aide/aide.db with 70,149 entries; confirmed aide.db and aide.db.new have identical md5sums, i.e. the baseline is correctly installed as the active database.

evidence.requirement: Baseline correctly reflects a clean, healthy /etc state (no false positives)
evidence.summary: Ran aide --check immediately after init; found differences only in ephemeral /run and /var/lib/lxcfs session/cgroup pseudo-files (created by our own SSH-like exec sessions), with zero differences under /etc/ (grep -c "/etc/" returned 0).

evidence.requirement: Baseline detects and reports later changes to files in /etc (core task requirement)
evidence.summary: Appended a marker line to /etc/hosts, ran aide.wrapper --check, and confirmed AIDE reported /etc/hosts as changed with detailed size/mtime/ctime/SHA256/SHA512/RMD160/TIGER/HAVAL/GOST/CRC32 before/after values, proving detection and reporting works.

evidence.requirement: Automated ongoing reporting mechanism exists (later changes can be 'reported')
evidence.summary: Confirmed /etc/cron.daily/aide exists (from aide-common package) which runs aide --check daily and reports differences automatically.

evidence.requirement: Restore system to clean baseline state after the detection demonstration
evidence.summary: Restored /etc/hosts to original content and re-ran aideinit to rebuild the baseline database reflecting the clean, restored state.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (a1dc8e25-9492-4e80-81a5-6337330a5f77) and ran aide.wrapper --check pre-restart, confirming zero differences under real /etc paths (only /run and lxcfs session churn).

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnection, and node polled back online
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded `sudo reboot`; acknowledgement returned; subsequent exec confirmed connection refused (node down); later exec succeeded confirming node1 back online.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proven (not just uptime)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 2e616fe5-1dc9-466c-a901-f588c73a88dd, differing from the pre-restart value a1dc8e25-9492-4e80-81a5-6337330a5f77, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required data/service verified
evidence.summary: Confirmed AIDE database file intact post-restart (identical md5sum to pre-restart), cron.service active, and a fresh aide --check post-restart showed zero real /etc/ differences (the only /etc/-matching diffs were postfix chroot copies under /var/spool/postfix/etc, refreshed on boot, not actual /etc files).
